Bad sectors cannot be fixed by reading or writing more data to the drive. Depending on the nature of the failure, reading and writing may cause more sectors to be damaged. Some attempts at repair may cause the drive to swap out failing sectors for spares, but that doesn't mean additional sectors won't go bad. A drive with manufacturing defects may manifest additional failing sectors over time. A drive with physical damage may wear out slowly causing you to mistakenly assume the damage "went away".
